blocks.text: Sulfur exhibits oxidation states of −2, 0, +2, +4, and +6. The electronic configuration of sulfur is depicted in Figure 12.8, where the oxidation state is determined by the number of unpaired electrons. Under standard conditions, sulfur and oxygen react to produce sulfur dioxide (SO₂) in which sulphur has an oxidation state of +4. However, to form sulfur trioxide (SO₃) with an oxidation state of +6, high energy is required.

blocks.alt: Orbital boxes in four rows. a) Oxygen ground state 2s2 2p4: no d-orbitals in 2nd shell, so excitation is not possible. b) Sulfur ground state 3s2 3p4 with five empty 3d boxes: 2+ oxidation state due to two unpaired electrons. c) Sulfur 1st excited state 3s2 3p3 3d1: 4+ due to four unpaired electrons. d) Sulphur second excited state 3s1 3p3 3d2: 6+ due to six unpaired electrons.
